markdownDescription:
## Model Creator Studio

Two models, built from tiles alone — no photo, no text prompt — each as a full identity sheet: a full-body card on grey, then a three-quarter, a portrait and a profile. Two rows side by side show what every tile does.

1. **Light** — the studio light from tiles, shared by both rows.
2. **Model A** — a Person picker with every dimension set (identity, body, face, hair, skin, eyes, features) and a Styling picker (makeup, hair cut, outfit, fabric).
3. **Model B** — the same two pickers with other choices. Compare the tiles, compare the pictures.
4. **Each row** — the pickers feed a model card; the card and the pickers feed three fixed framings, so the face never drifts.
5. Wire a model card into any other template as the model reference — it is the anchor every shot is measured against.

data.text: Studio light from tiles, shared by both rows. Soft high-key three-quarter light shows the face and the skin honestly — the right light for a reference sheet.
data.label: Step 1
data.title: 1 · Light

data.text: Read the row left to right. Person: every dimension is set from tiles — type, age, heritage, frame, waist, hips, face shape, jaw, cheekbones, eyes, nose, lips, hair, brows, skin, features. Styling: makeup, hair cut and treatment, hair state, outfit, top, fabric. Both feed the model card, a full-body reference on grey; the card and the pickers then feed three fixed framings. Open a picker to see the tiles; change one and rerun the row to watch the picture follow.
data.label: Step 2
data.title: 2 · Model a — tiles → Card → Three framings

data.text: A second person from the same two pickers: another type, a broad frame, a strong jaw, tan sun-kissed skin, stubble, dimples, a Hawaiian island aesthetic, silver jewellery, a t-shirt and shorts. The row is identical to Model A's — only the tiles differ. This is the whole idea: the model is a set of choices, not a photo you have to find.
